newsitem.title: USA: King World proceeds in suit against Sony.
newsitem.headline: King World proceeds in suit against Sony.

text.p: King World Productions Inc said Tuesday it is proceeding in its pending litigation with the two subsidiaries of Sony Pictures Entertainment that produce "Wheel of Fortune" and "Jeopardy!"

On March 24, King World filed an action in California Superior Court, Los Angeles County, against those companies, seeking to confirm its rights to produce and license others to produce strip game shows for distribution in first-run syndication by others. The company said the right to do so is explicitly recognized in its distribution agreements.

On May 8, 1997, King World said the defendants filed an answer and cross-complaint, which alleges that it has breached the distribution agreements with the defendants and seeks a judgement for damages in an unspecified amount, for termination of the distribution agreements and/or for reformation (in effect, a judicial rewriting) of the agreements to prohibit King World from, among other things, producing any strip game show for first-run syndication.

King World said it believes that the allegations of the cross-complaint are wholly without merit. It said it has never taken any action that would breach the agreements under which it distributes "Wheel of Fortune" and "Jeopardy!" and that Sony's request that the court rewrite the agreements reflects the fact that the unambiguous language of the agreements acknowledges its right to produce and license others to produce a strip game show for distribution in first-run syndication by others.
Sony Pictures said it does not comment on matters in litigation.
